turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. ____. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um, well, I guess what finally made me come in is... it's probably not a huge deal, but I've been having some trouble with these really silly mistakes. Like, I'll turn in applications or, um, my research notes, and there will be these minor but kind of embarrassing errors in them. Like I might mislabel an artwork date, or just completely skip a question by accident. 

And the thing is, I honestly thought I had checked everything really carefully before handing it in. It makes me look a bit careless, which I really try not to be... I don't know, is that the kind of thing people usually come here for? I hope I'm explaining that okay.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly describes making careless, minor mistakes on applications and research notes, such as mislabeling dates or skipping questions, despite believing they had checked their work carefully.

turns.doctor_question: Do you also make these kinds of careless mistakes in everyday tasks at home, like bills, appointments, or leaving things unfinished?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah, a little bit, I guess. I mean, I really try to stay on top of things, I promise. But sometimes... well, I'll fully mean to do just, you know, normal adult things? Like returning an email, or paying a bill, or even just picking up groceries. And then, a few days will go by, and I'll suddenly realize I never actually did it. 

It’s like it just completely drops out of my mind. It’s definitely not because I don't care, I really do try to be responsible. I just... get sidetracked, I think? I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly lazy or anything. Does that make sense?

symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly confirms forgetting to do everyday tasks like returning emails, paying bills, and picking up groceries, stating these tasks completely drop out of their mind.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have similar attention or organization problems as a child, before age 12?
turns.patient_response:
Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a really good kid, I promise, and I loved learning. But, um... I suppose even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I had, you know, really good ideas and everything. It's just that sometimes I would... well, forget to turn in a worksheet, or maybe misplace the instructions for an assignment. 

And I'd sometimes miss little details on things, unless my parents went through my backpack with me every night to make sure everything was there. But I really did try my best, and my teachers always said I was a pleasure to have in class! I just needed a little extra help staying organized, I think. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for?

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions missing little details on things during elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient states they would forget to turn in worksheets, indicating difficulty following through on schoolwork.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly notes they needed extra help staying organized.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient mentions misplacing instructions for assignments.

turns.doctor_question: Do you also have trouble focusing when you’re just listening to someone talk or reading something for fun?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, I don't think so? I mean, I try really hard to be a good listener. If someone is talking to me, I really want to hear what they have to say, and I try to give them my full attention. 

And as for reading for fun, I actually really enjoy it! I mean, I might not read as fast as some people, but I don't think I have a hard time focusing on it. If it's something I'm interested in, I can usually just sit and read it without any problems. I hope that's okay? I mean, I don't want to seem like I'm making a big deal out of nothing, but I just don't think I really struggle with that part.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having a hard time focusing on reading for fun, stating they can sit and read without problems.
symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient denies having trouble listening to others, stating they try to give their full attention when someone is talking to them.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying a lot most days?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I worry a lot. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude about things, you know? 

I mean, sure, I get a little stressed sometimes, like anyone else, especially when I realize I've forgotten something important. But it's not like I'm constantly anxious or worrying all day every day. I really try to just take things as they come and not let things get to me too much. I hope that makes sense? I just don't think I'm a very, um, anxious person in general.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying a lot or being constantly anxious, stating they try to keep a positive attitude and take things as they come.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling down, sad, or depressed most days lately?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, definitely not. I mean, I really try to stay upbeat and look on the bright side of things! 

I guess I get a little frustrated with myself sometimes when I mess up or, you know, lose track of time, but I wouldn't call it being depressed. I'm actually a pretty happy person, I promise. I really like to keep a smile on my face and not let things drag me down. Is it okay that I don't feel sad like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling down, sad, or depressed, stating they are a pretty happy person and try to stay upbeat.
